questions.q: Why aren't naming conventions (Lesson 34) enough documentation on their own?
options: A name communicates a column's role (e.g. surrogate key) but not its meaning, such as units, currency, or exactly when a flag gets set
Naming conventions are only used during development and are removed before production
SQL Server does not allow named columns in a warehouse
Naming conventions replace the need for any keys or constraints
questions.explain: ProductKey clearly signals a surrogate key, but nothing about the name tells you whether StandardCost is in US dollars or a local currency — that needs real documentation.

questions.q: What does SSMS's Database Diagram tool do?
options: Draws a real entity-relationship diagram directly from a live schema, showing tables, keys, and relationship lines automatically
Automatically writes ETL pipelines for the tables shown
Deletes tables that have no foreign key relationships
Only works with Azure SQL Database, never on-premises SQL Server
questions.explain: Adding tables to a new database diagram in SSMS lays each one out with its columns, primary-key markers, and the foreign-key relationship lines connecting them, straight from the live schema.

options: Attaching arbitrary name/value metadata, like a description, directly to a table, column, or other database object
Creating a new index on a table
Adding a new physical column to a table
Granting permissions to a database user
questions.explain: Extended properties (commonly named MS_Description) let you pin documentation directly onto database objects, where many tools display it automatically.

questions.q: Why is metadata stored via sp_addextendedproperty considered more durable than a description kept in a separate wiki page or Word document?
options: It lives inside the database itself, so it travels with the schema, survives a restore, and is directly queryable
Extended properties are automatically emailed to the whole team every time they change
sp_addextendedproperty descriptions cannot be edited once created, so they can't go stale
Extended properties replace the need for a CREATE TABLE statement
questions.explain: Because the metadata is part of the database, it moves with a restore or copy and can be queried with sys.fn_listextendedproperty, unlike an external document that can silently go stale.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should a complete warehouse data dictionary entry for a table record, beyond column names?
options: The table's grain, each column's business meaning/unit/source, SCD type for changing attributes, and load frequency/ETL job
Only the table's physical file size on disk
The exact server hardware the database runs on
Nothing beyond what a naming convention already communicates
questions.explain: Putting the course's earlier lessons together, a real data dictionary entry needs the grain, business meaning of each column, SCD type where relevant, and how/how-often the table is loaded.
